evidence.method: Read retained Chat bytes; inject dated events into an isolated synthetic SessionManager record; call actual private snapshot/append methods. No original Run or source repair.

confirmedProblems.classification: BGS host implementation / synchronous nested history scans
confirmedProblems.cause: Each appended stream event persisted a snapshot. Phase calculation scanned all events for every previous turn, and phaseStatus called it again twice. Offline profile showed 69.3% inclusive samples on this nested phase path.
confirmedProblems.fix: Collect started/ended turn identities in one linear pass, compute phase once and reuse it. Preserve terminal-before-start/missing-turn-ID/failed/waiting-approval/recovered behavior. Status is not writer exit proof.

confirmedProblems.classification: BGS host implementation / repeated work on non-statistical stream details
confirmedProblems.cause: Even the linear phase patch still recomputed full usage/roles over all preceding detail events for every new text fragment.
confirmedProblems.fix: Per-session weak append-only snapshot-input index coalesces only consecutive assistant.partial/assistant.thinking/tool.progress of the same turn to their last boundary. All lifecycle, permission, accounting, tools and unknown types remain. Original events/transcripts/Agent history unchanged; same index speeds stale-turn guard.
confirmedProblems.addedComplexityReason: Linear phase alone left this replay at 1.91s/100 appends; a 19-line method + weak reference index avoids known repeated detail scans without rewriting accounting or introducing a scheduler/authority store.
confirmedProblems.boundaries: This is a derived host status index, not Agent context compaction, raw Chat filtering or a recovery fact. All accounting checkpoints and full Question provenance remain authoritative.

confirmedProblems.classification: BGS native transport adapter / event-loop starvation
confirmedProblems.cause: Ordered stdout consumption awaited callbacks that often resolved immediately; microtasks drained queued frames before timers/HTTP. With the first two fixes present, the real adapter/fixture still delivered all 500 frames before loopback health or explicit interrupt.
confirmedProblems.fix: One setImmediate yield after each ordered native message in the BGS adapter. No frame count limit, dropped output, reordered native frames, retry, business stage or provider/Claude Code query-loop edit.
confirmedProblems.sideEffect: Control callbacks can now interleave with frame processing; small host scheduling overhead. EOF draining, permissions, background ownership, cancellation and final stderr accounting regressed.

sameReplay.limits: Snapshot/append synchronous host work plus a timer, not end-to-end production/model/Token cost or an SLA.

queuedStdoutHTTP.limits: Real BGS manager/native adapter and loopback probe, but fixed CLI fixture, not the production dashboard/API, paid model or external engine.

redTests.correctedInstrumentation: Type-only read counting originally missed short-circuit turn-ID comparisons. Added actual turnId getter operations, preserving functional assertions; no production behavior changed to fit the test.
redTests.approvalTimeout: The first loopback test permission review timed out before a process started. Tool permitted one diagnostic retry; not a BGS execution/model retry.

remaining: Not deployed; normal runtime code remains 1.78. No paid rerun or actual stalled project's recovery/work was initiated.

The original unsymbolized incident sample alone cannot prove these were the only cause of every historical stall; this replay proves concrete host defects under the retained history and native queued-frame conditions.
Cold transcript parsing, extremely large individual frames, long-term growth of meaningful events, filesystem stalls, external tools/providers and whole-machine failures are not all certified.
No native context reduction, real Token savings, full eight-domain game/Scene/UI/assets/art/audio quality, engine deliverability or formal frontend completion claimed.
Further checks must follow concrete evidence, not arbitrary history/turn limits, prompt stacking or a new workflow framework.
